page: Amazon Web Services r5n.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with x86_64 architecture, offering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage or GPU bundled with this instance, meaning it relies entirely on network-attached storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average multi-core performance but weaker single-core capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test scored 13544.27, and the Geekbench multi-core score reached 7004.0, both falling into the middle 50% tier. Conversely, single-core metrics such as the Geekbench single-core score of 1122.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 21.82 GB/sec are positioned in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is solid, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 753.69 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 48.4 GB/sec. Database operations via Passmark scored 5270.92, and Redis SET operations achieved 13.18 million operations per second, reflecting stable performance for memory-bound tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5n.4xlarge provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive applications without the overhead of local NVMe storage. The dedicated CPU allocation and Nitro hypervisor ensure consistent performance. This instance is best suited for workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers, medium-scale database operations, and memory-heavy data processing pipelines that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance.
